image_description: A side-profile view of a Triceratops dinosaur model or illustration. The creature is quadrupedal with a large, solid bony frill featuring marginal bumps (epoccipitals). It has two prominent brow horns and a smaller nasal horn. The skin texture appears rough and scaled, with a row of quill-like or spine-like structures running along the back. The forelimbs are visible and appear shorter than the hindquarters, creating a sloping backline. The image quality is low-resolution and slightly blurry.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (no holes/fenestrations). Distinct bumps are visible along the upper margin of the frill, matching the description of epoccipitals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is rough and pebbled, consistent with scales. A distinct row of spine/quill-like protrusions runs along the dorsal line from the neck to the tail base.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shoulder height is visibly lower than the hip height, resulting in a downward slope from rear to front, which is anatomically correct for Triceratops.
The tail extends out of the frame to the right; only the very base near the hind legs is potentially visible, making full verification impossible.
